headline: Dollar hits 52-week high on Fed hike bets, sinking copper and WTI 4.7% and gold 3.1%
subhead: Gold and silver closed at 52-week lows as futures priced about a 95 percent chance of a December hike, while Nvidia fell 2.9% to its own 52-week low of 150.96 despite beating estimates and Anthropic priced its record IPO at 83 dollars.

us.text: S&P 500 fell 0.2% to 7,323.6 for a fifth straight loss and the Dow lost 1.1% to 50,198.2 on health insurers and energy; Nasdaq rose 0.4%.
Nvidia fell 2.9% to a 52-week low of 150.96 despite beating estimates, as its board ruled out reinstating Jensen Huang and delayed its 10-Q.
Anthropic priced its IPO at 83 dollars, above the 70 to 78 range, raising about 81 billion dollars; Amazon rose 3.8% and UnitedHealth fell 10.2% on a CMS audit rule.

india.text: Nifty fell about 160 points to below 25,250 on Wednesday on profit booking and metal stocks; the price feed still shows Tuesday's 25,387.4.
FIIs net bought about 4,195 crore rupees in cash on Tuesday and DIIs about 197 crore, a second straight day of foreign buying.
Rupee ended flat at 93.44 per dollar on Wednesday after touching a seven-month high, as global dollar strength offset foreign inflows.

global.text: Nikkei 225 rose 0.3% to 59,053 as an early lift from Nvidia's beat faded, with about 71 percent of Prime stocks falling.
STOXX 600 fell 1.75% on Tuesday, its worst day in eight months, as SAP and Deutsche Bank led the DAX down 2.1%.
Dollar index rose 0.3% to a 52-week high of 103.8 as Waller floated a half-point hike; WTI crude fell 4.7% after a US stock build.

weekly.narrative: Jensen Huang's sudden exit as Nvidia CEO dominated the week: Nvidia fell 12.8 percent, but rotation into Apple, AMD and Broadcom still left the S&P 500 up 2.5 percent and the Nasdaq up 2.3 percent despite a Friday AI selloff. Hot US CPI and 6.5 percent annual PPI pushed the 10-year yield to 5.15 percent and left a December Fed hike fully priced, lifting the dollar to a 19-month high. That weighed on metals and crypto: gold fell 4.5 percent to a 13-month low, silver 6.1 percent and bitcoin broke below 70,000 dollars. India leaned on nine straight sessions of foreign buying and a bank rally, though the Nifty slipped to 25,144.3 on Friday after October CPI rose to 6.09 percent. Next week brings Nvidia results on 17 November, FOMC minutes on 18 November and Anthropic's expected Nasdaq debut on 19 November.
